name: Samoan Myzomela
rangeDescription: Samoa (upolu, savai'i, and tutuila)
description: A small, strikingly plumaged myzomela with a bright crimson-red head, chest, back, and rump and black wings, belly, and tail. Thin bill decurved.

name: Red Fody
rangeDescription: Madagascar; introduced reunion, mauritius, seychelles, rodrigues, amirantes, and chagos islands (indian ocean); also on st. helena (atlantic ocean); and bahrain (arabian peninsula); present also on glorieuses and comoro islands (indian ocean)
description: Sparrow-like weaver in which scarlet breeding males are distinctive, but females and non-breeding females very drab. Found in virtually all habitats except the interior of thick forest.

name: Long-wattled Umbrellabird
rangeDescription: Western andes of southwestern colombia and western ecuador (south to el oro)
description: Spectacular crow-like bird with a bushy crest. Male has a thick feathered wattle dangling from his throat that can be extended to an astonishing length while displaying.

name: Red-throated Sunbird
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern myanmar, southern peninsular thailand, malaya, sumatra, and borneo
description: Medium-sized sunbird with a fairly straight dark bill. Brightly-colored has an iridescent green back, yellowish belly, and reddish wings, face, and throat.

name: Trocaz Pigeon
rangeDescription: Laurel forest of madeira
description: Endemic to the island of Madeira, where it is largely restricted to native laurel and tree heath forests. Body is largely gray with a purple-pink breast, and a noticeable silvery patch with black streaks on the side of the neck.

name: Red-throated Thrush
rangeDescription: Eastern siberia to northern manchuria; winters to western china, myanmar, and northeastern india
description: This eastern counterpart of the Black-throated Thrush also breeds in montane areas and winters in lower-elevation areas on average. Males gray above and white below, with a brick-red throat and supercilium.

name: Chiriqui Foliage-gleaner
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of southwestern costa rica to western panama (chiriquí)
description: Skulking and generally inconspicuous brown bird of humid tropical forest. Found as singles or pairs, clambering in vine tangles or other dense understory, at times in leaf litter on the forest floor; usually difficult to see clearly.

name: Tanimbar Starling
rangeDescription: Tanimbar islands (larat and yamdena)
description: A uniformly blackish starling with a medium-length square tail and a dark eye. Juveniles browner, with streaking below and a rufous-tinged tail.

name: Sooty-faced Finch
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of costa rica and western panama; a population on cerro tacarcuna in far eastern panama and adjacent colombia usually considered part of this species, but genetically is closer to olive finch arremon castaneiceps
description: Medium-sized sparrowlike bird; olive overall with contrasting yellow belly, white mustache line, dark gray face, and rufous cap. Range does not overlap with other similar-looking sparrows and brushfinches.

name: Booted Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern palearctic; winters to india and sri lanka
description: Small, recalling a beige chiffchaff or other Phylloscopus warbler. Rather nondescript: gray brown above, paler below, with a short, dark-tipped bill and conspicuous pale eyebrow.

name: Black Grasswren
rangeDescription: Sandstones of western kimberley division (western australia)
description: Small chestnut-and-black bird with a long tail, found in areas with large rocky sandstone boulders and dense spinifex grass of the northwestern Kimberley region of Western Australia, with most sightings from the Mitchell Plateau. Rich chestnut-brown above, black below, the head and breast liberally streaked with white.

name: Crab-Plover
rangeDescription: Coastal northern indian ocean; ranges to madagascar and andaman islands
description: Utterly unmistakable large shorebird: gleaming white adult has a black back, black flight feathers, and a very heavy dark bill, which is used to dispatch crustaceans and other invertebrates. Narrow dark smudge around the eye imparts a sleepy appearance.

name: Naung Mung Scimitar-Babbler
rangeDescription: Sub-himalayan myanmar
description: Strange short-tailed babbler with a long decurved bill. Currently only known from the far northern tip of Myanmar, and potentially adjacent border regions of southwestern China.

name: Taliabu Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Taliabu island (sula islands)
description: A recently described species endemic to the declining montane forests of Taliabu. Dark, sparrow-sized warbler with a scruffy-looking, graduated tail.

name: Eared Quetzal
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western mexico; occasional southeastern arizona
description: Scarce, large trogon of pine and pine-oak forests in mountains and canyons of northwest Mexico. Usually rather wary, flying long distances when disturbed, but can be found feeding quietly at fruiting trees.

name: African Desert Warbler
rangeDescription: Desert of northwestern africa to eastern libya
description: Very small Sylvia warbler of sandy desert with scattered low shrubs. Plumage is a pale warm buff-brown overall; warmer than the closely-related Asian Desert Warbler that has more prominently-patterned tertials.

name: Taiwan Yuhina
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: A small, tit-like endemic songbird, brown above, white below, with a very distinctive head pattern: the pointed crest is white with a black-bordered chestnut front, and the ear coverts are outlined in black on the white face. Inhabits hilly and montane forests, where it roams about in large chattering flocks at all levels of the forest.

name: Sao Tome Ibis
rangeDescription: São tomé island (gulf of guinea)
description: Very small, dark forest-dwelling ibis. Note the dark blue bare skin on the face, the ragged crest, and the glossy green shoulders.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Finsch's Francolin
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed in congo, southwestern democratic republic of the congo and central angola
description: Medium-sized francolin with a mostly gray body, rufous head, and white throat. Found locally on the ground in grassy habitats including savanna, montane grassland, and woodland.

name: Baudo Oropendola
rangeDescription: Northeastern colombia (northern chocó)
description: This impressively large and colorful oropendola is found only in lowland and foothill rainforest in northwestern Colombia. Its salmon-colored cheek patches along with chestnut back and belly distinguish it from Black Oropendola; also note the yellow tail and orange bill tip.
